cleared.check: L-1129, the rule. How the HyperEVM archive client nanoreth (tag nb-20261125-2) decides that a transaction is a system transaction and where it takes the sender from.
cleared.result: A transaction is a system transaction when gas_price() is Some(0) (src/node/primitives/transaction.rs:182-184, src/node/evm/executor.rs:44-49). For such a transaction recover_signer, recover_signer_unchecked and recover_unchecked_with_buf return s_to_address(s): s equal to 1 gives 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, s equal to (1<<160)|1 gives 0x00..01, and any other s gives its low 20 bytes (transaction.rs:49-58 and 77-97). The file header calls this a pseudo signer for system transactions, and address_to_s (transaction.rs:61-69) is the encoder. The system transactions come from the block source as a separate list system_txs with an optional from field (src/node/types/mod.rs:114-128 and 285-290), and the official endpoint serves them under its own method eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber. The synthetic signature is therefore the replica's encoding of what the producer wrote, not a rule that any public endpoint applies to a signed transaction a user submits. If the producer ever put a regular transaction with gas price 0 into a block, the replica would take its sender from s and show state the producer did not compute; that would mislead replica readers and would not change the chain. Under EIP-1559 such a transaction is invalid because the base fee is nonzero in every block read. The cycle 23 census of mined blocks found none below 100,000,000 wei; during verification eth_feeHistory predicted 96,659,059 and 89,439,317 wei for a next block, so 100,000,000 is not a confirmed protocol floor, and any nonzero base fee is enough here. The producer's own admission rule is closed and was not read; no Hyperliquid page that states it was found.

cleared.check: L-1129, the blocks since the MRB fork. 2,000 blocks drawn uniformly from 50,988,232 (MRB activation) to 52,328,897 with seed 2027027, read in full on rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 before and after), with eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm ('hyperliquid evm Mainnet' before and after) for every tenth block.
cleared.result: 10,771 transactions, of which 1,096 in 661 blocks have gas price 0. All 1,096 are type 0, and in all 1,096 the from field equals the address decoded from s. The 38 senders are 0x2222...2222 (16 native HYPE credits), 35 token system addresses of the form 0x20 followed by the token index (433), and the two AQAv2 addresses that cycle 23 already recorded under F-020: 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24, the USDC linked contract (427), and 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00, the USDC treasury (220). None has the PoolManager 0x12D4Fd9C...6B1F as sender, target or first argument. For all 200 compared blocks the official system transaction list has the same senders, targets and selectors in the same order as the replica. The PoolManager nonce is 1 on the official endpoint. So since the fork no gas price 0 transaction has run in the name of the PoolManager or of an account without a HyperCore role, and the only senders outside 0x2222 and 0x20.. are the two AQAv2 addresses whose case F-020 covers.

cleared.check: Task 1 test: eth_call and eth_estimateGas with from set to the PoolManager and gasPrice 0, with value 0 and 1 wei, plus an extsload read, on every network (endpoints of networks.json, web3_clientVersion before and after; Ethereum and Polygon repeated on eth.drpc.org and polygon.drpc.org after HTTP 403 from publicnode).
cleared.result: Every endpoint accepts from = PoolManager at gas price 0. eth_call of a plain call returns 0x and eth_estimateGas returns 21,000 (Arbitrum One 21,305, Robinhood Chain 21,292, MegaETH 60,000) on all 21; value 1 wei is accepted on the 20 networks with native value, and Tempo refuses value with 'value transfer not allowed' (-32003). This shows only that the simulation layer skips the EIP-3607 code check and the fee check, as these methods are specified to; it does not show that a transaction from the PoolManager can be signed, admitted or mined. The PoolManager nonce is 1 on 20 networks and 0 on Unichain, where it is a genesis predeploy; no transaction has used it as sender anywhere. No public read-only method takes a signed raw transaction and reports the sender that a producer would derive, so the HyperEVM part of L-1129 that asks for a raw transaction with the PoolManager as derived sender has no read-only test.

cleared.check: OP Stack deposits and aliasing (OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, MegaETH): can an ordinary L1 account produce a deposit whose L2 sender is the PoolManager.
cleared.result: No. The portal sets from to msg.sender only when EOA.isSenderEOA() holds, that is msg.sender == tx.origin, or code of exactly 23 bytes that starts with 0xEF0100 (an EIP-7702 delegation); otherwise from is the L1 to L2 alias (OptimismPortal2.sol:939-943, EOA.sol:9-24 on the develop branch). EIP-3541 forbids deployed code starting with 0xEF, so a contract cannot pass the check, and the first two cases need a key for the L1 address. The PoolManager addresses and their alias preimages have no code and nonce 0 on Ethereum (F-140), and finding a key or CREATE2 input for a chosen 160-bit address costs about 2^160. Only a portal upgrade by its upgrader can emit such a deposit, which F-140 records at governance level.

cleared.check: Tempo type 0x76: can a batch, a Keychain signature, a key authorization, a fee payer, a Tempo authorization list or a configurable account make the PoolManager the sender (tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748 answers on the endpoint; source tree of v1.19.1 read).
cleared.result: No. The sender is the address derived from a secp256k1, P256 or WebAuthn public key (spec, Address Derivation). A Keychain signature names user_address, prepare_keychain rejects it unless it equals the recovered signer, and the access key must be registered for that account in AccountKeychain (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:655-676). A key authorization must be signed by the root key of the account or by an admin access key already registered for it, with account equal to the signer (handler.rs:504-627). A configurable account role is refused when the account has code other than the configurable account code (valid_account_code, crates/precompiles/src/configurable_account/mod.rs:272-279, used in handler/configurable_account/mod.rs:350-356), and without a stored commitment its address must equal the hash derivation of the config (crates/primitives/src/transaction/configurable_account/mod.rs:384-414). The PoolManager has 24,009 bytes of code and no key, so none of these paths can name it. A fee payer pays fees and never becomes a caller, and every call of a batch has the one signer as caller (cycle 21 clearances).

cleared.check: Task 1 across networks: which senders the PoolManager trusts and whether any network-level sender can be made equal to the PoolManager, a router or a holder of claims or positions by an ordinary account.
cleared.result: The PoolManager keys deltas, claims, allowances, operators and positions on msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:110, 161, 183, 226, 270, 294, 301, 311-317, 326, 334; src/ERC6909.sol:26-61; position owner in src/libraries/Position.sol:48-56), so whoever is CALLER owns those records. Per network: Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc: no (cycle 20 client readings, F-058, Arc CallFrom limited to tx.origin). OP Stack and Celo, X Layer, MegaETH deposits: no for ordinary accounts, governance only (F-140, item above). Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium: unsigned messages and retryables are aliased for every L1 caller, only governance can post a contract transaction as the PoolManager (F-138). HyperEVM: no; system transaction senders are HyperCore system addresses and the two AQAv2 addresses (F-020 covers the operator case). Tempo: no (item above). EIP-7702 on every network that has it: an authority must sign, and an authority whose code is not a delegation is skipped, so the PoolManager cannot be delegated; an EOA that holds claims or positions and delegates gives its own records to the delegate code it chose. No precompile on the 21 networks forwards a call with a caller chosen by its input (Arc CallFrom checks tx.origin; HyperEVM CoreWriter takes actions for its caller only).

cleared.check: Task 2: what one party of a shared transaction can leave for a later party through the transient state of sync (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36), and whether any of it moves funds.
cleared.result: Only the synced currency and its reserves outlive a call; unlock clears the lock flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Left behind, a synced token makes a later native settle revert with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), which F-071 records as low. A stale reserve R makes a later settle without its own sync credit balanceOf minus R: if the balance fell since (a take), the subtraction reverts (checked arithmetic, src/PoolManager.sol:360); if it rose, the extra is a payment some account made to the PoolManager after that sync without settling it, which is the first party's own gift or the F-137 pattern. resetCurrency clears only the currency slot (CurrencyReserves.sol:21-25), and sync writes currency and reserves together (CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so no sequence pairs a currency with a reserve from another moment. Nothing moves funds of pools or claim holders. Clearing between transactions was shown on 16 networks with eth_simulateV1 in cycle 21; Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM still have no eth_simulateV1 today, so they rest on the client readings of earlier cycles.

cleared.check: Task 3 and 4: the four outgoing shapes (value call with empty calldata, transfer, balanceOf, hook selector) sent from the PoolManager address to every listed precompile, predeploy and system contract.
cleared.result: Already measured: cycle 13 calleegas.py on all 21 networks and L-166 with balances read before and after. Reanalysed here from cycle 13 raw data: transfer returns success with no return data at addresses without code, at precompiles 0x01 and 0x100 and several system addresses, which src/types/Currency.sol:60-80 treats as success; such a take debits the caller in that currency id and moves nothing, so the loss is the caller's own. 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 return a 32 byte word for balanceOf, so they can be synced as currencies with nonsense reserves, which only affects pools whose creator named them. 0x04 echoes every hook selector but fails the hook address check (Hooks.sol:109-124, cycle 13). The real currencies with a second face (Celo CELO token, Polygon 0x1010, Arc USDC 0x3600) were walked in earlier cycles without a double credit. No answer registers, stakes, bridges or burns in the PoolManager's name except the native payout cases of F-021, F-047, F-048 and F-049, which lose only the caller's payout. Balance rises outside a transfer can be booked between a sync and a settle only when the rise is triggered inside the same transaction: system credits on HyperEVM run as separate transactions, native value is never credited without msg.value, and the bridge and token cases are F-137 and the token findings.

leads.question: Does Hyperliquid publish the validator's admission rule for a legacy transaction with gas price 0, or any statement that only HyperCore can emit transactions in the system list?
leads.why: The replica takes the sender of any gas price 0 transaction from its s value. The closed producer is the only party that decides inclusion, and its rule is unpublished, so the safety of this path rests on the base fee check and the observed census.

leadResults.answer: nanoreth nb-20261125-2 treats a type 0 or 1 transaction with gas price 0 as a system transaction and takes its sender from the low 20 bytes of s (transaction.rs:49-58, 77-97, 182-184). This encodes the producer's separate system transaction list and is not applied to user submissions by any public endpoint. In 2,000 seeded blocks since MRB, all 1,096 gas price 0 transactions come from 0x2222..22, 35 token system addresses or the two AQAv2 addresses already in F-020; none names the PoolManager, from equals the s-decoded address in all, and 200 of 200 official system lists match. eth_call and eth_estimateGas accept from = PoolManager at gas price 0 on HyperEVM and all other networks, which proves nothing about inclusion; no read-only method tests a raw transaction with the PoolManager as derived sender.
